The raw column was renamed from `amount` to `txn_amount`. The profile shows `txn_amount` as DOUBLE, and no `amount` column exists. The values look like the same dollar amounts, all USD, with a plausible range, so this is a plain rename and the fix is safe.

The fix is to cast `txn_amount` to DECIMAL(12,2) in silver_transactions. The rest of the SQL stays unchanged. Casting a DOUBLE such as 36.11 to DECIMAL(12,2) rounds correctly.

The status filter is still valid, since the values are POSTED and REVERSED. There are no duplicates, because txn_id is distinct across all 4802 rows.

The amounts have at most 2 decimals, as the samples show, so nothing is lost in the cast.

Point the cast at txn_amount.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.93, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(txn_amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
